SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.

2. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

3. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

4. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Producers
   D. Tertiary consumers

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

8. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. watt (W)

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.

10. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

11. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

12. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

13. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

15. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
